 Curry's Injury Update Plan For Injuries Inside The Timberwolves Knicks Need KAT Power Rankings Stephen Curry gets MRI after suffering abdomen injury vs. Rockets: ‘The concern is high’
 Stephen Curry left in the first quarter of Wednesday's game in Houston. Ashley Landis / Associated Press 
 By Nick Friedell Nov. 11, 2026 Updated Nov. 12, 2026 2:24 am EST Share article 35 HOUSTON — Golden State Warriors star guard Stephen Curry got an MRI after leaving Wednesday’s 115-108 loss to the Houston Rockets early in the first quarter with right abdominal soreness.
 Warriors coach Steve Kerr said that it was unclear exactly when Curry suffered the injury. Curry went back to the locker room after the first timeout of the game, with 6:25 remaining in the first quarter.
 Advertisement
 He was visibly frustrated after knocking down his only shot of the night. Curry spoke to Kerr for a couple of seconds before exiting the floor with a member of the Warriors’ training staff and never returned.
 “The concern is high,” Kerr said after the game. “But I have no idea the extent of the injury.”
 Kerr said he didn’t know exactly when Curry suffered the injury.
 “He just said he tweaked something in his abdominal area and said he’s never done it before,” Kerr said. “And he went to get an MRI tonight. We haven’t heard anything about the results … I just saw him holding his side and tried to get him out as quickly as I could.”
 Stephen Curry headed to the locker room with an apparent right hip injury. pic.twitter.com/1zVrNz00bH 
 — ESPN (@espn) November 12, 2026 
 The 38-year-old Curry has been at his peak in the early stages of the season and is the biggest reason the Warriors came into Houston having won eight straight games. Curry entered Wednesday’s matchup averaging 30.6 points, 4.3 assists and 4.1 rebounds.
 Warriors guard Will Richard said Curry spoke to the team at halftime. “He made sure everybody knew he was OK,” Richard said.
 Stephen Curry left the court in the first quarter. (Ashley Landis / Associated Press) With Curry potentially out in the short-term, greater focus will be on rookie big man Yaxel Lendeborg and young guard Brandin Podziemski as the Warriors head to San Antonio to face Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs on Friday night.
 Lendeborg had 25 points and 10 rebounds in Wednesday’s loss and will draw even more attention if Curry misses any time.
 Warriors forward Draymond Green made an interesting point regarding what Lendeborg may have figured out in Wednesday’s game.
 “It’s funny because the thing that he’s going to have to learn and understand is, all right, Steph wasn’t out there, KD (Kevin Durant) was off the court, you look around, you’re probably the best player on the floor. Regardless of team.
 Advertisement
 “I think there was a point he realized, ding, ding ding, and he started attacking, and the game flipped for us. I think that’s something that he’s going to have to realize really fast. There will be oftentimes where can possibly be the best player on the floor regardless of the team. We need him to show that. He doesn’t have a problem doing it.”
 Top Plays from Warriors @ Rockets Both Green and Podziemski sounded confident that the Warriors were better equipped to handle Curry’s potential absence than they were a year ago, especially given that most of this roster was together when Curry had to miss several months because of a lingering knee issue.
 “There’s a lot of familiarity with playing without him,” Podziemski said. “So we’re going to figure it out. We’re a confident group. We can’t let one player, as good as he is, kind of let our season go down. So we just got to figure it out and find ways to win games.”
